# prime-toast

prime-rs: Toast component and MessageService (PrimeNG port)

[Live demo](https://anton-avramchuk.github.io/prime-rs/toast) · [API docs](https://docs.rs/prime-toast) · [Port notes](https://github.com/anton-avramchuk/prime-rs/blob/HEAD/docs/toast.md)

Toast and `MessageService` — port of `p-toast` and `MessageService` from PrimeNG 21.1.10.

Notifications in a screen corner. The app sends messages to the shared `MessageService` (kept in context), and `Toast` components
show those addressed to their `key`. Messages close on their own via `life`, via the button and via `clear`; hovering pauses the
timer.

```rust
use leptos::prelude::*;
use prime_toast::{Toast, ToastMessage, ToastSeverity, provide_message_service};

Owner::new().with(|| {
    let service = provide_message_service();
    let html = view! { <Toast /> }.to_html();
    // no messages on the server: an empty container is rendered
    assert!(html.contains("p-toast") && !html.contains("p-toast-message"));
    service.add(ToastMessage::new(ToastSeverity::Success, "Saved", "Done"));
});
```

## Installation

```toml
[dependencies]
prime-toast = "0.1"
prime-theme = { version = "0.1", features = ["toast"] }
```

The component renders PrimeNG classes; its styles come from `prime-theme` (the Aura theme), one feature per component.
For server rendering enable the `ssr` feature in the server build and `hydrate` in the browser build.
Setting up an application (theme, SSR and hydration): https://anton-avramchuk.github.io/prime-rs/install
